forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be the polynomial ring graded by deg(x_s) = s for each s in I. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. Assume M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Then there exists a family (f_s)_{s in I} of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I, and the ordered list of these polynomials in increasing order of s is a regular sequence in R. If I is empty, this means the empty family.

result_payload.proof_summary: I could not complete a self-contained proof from the allowed context. The natural candidate family is to take f_s to be the coefficient of T^{r+s} in the formal series 1/(1-\sum_{t=a+1}^b (-1)^{t-1} x_t T^t); in small cases this produces the expected examples (for instance, for weights 2 and 3 one gets x_2x_3 and x_2^3+x_3^2). The remaining step is to prove rigorously that these candidates always form a regular sequence under the interval divisibility hypothesis M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for all d>0. I was not able to establish that step self-containedly.

suspected_gaps: I could not prove from the allowed context the weighted complete-intersection existence criterion that this lemma is expressing.

I could not give a self-contained argument that the natural complete-homogeneous candidates have common zero-locus only at the origin, or otherwise have height |I|, under the stated counting hypothesis.

result_payload.stuck_point: A standard route would be to invoke a known external theorem (often attributed to Kac-Watanabe / Watanabe) giving a necessary-and-sufficient divisibility criterion for the existence of a homogeneous regular sequence of prescribed degrees in a weighted polynomial ring. Your hypothesis is exactly the interval form of that criterion. But that theorem is not present in the allowed context, and I could not rederive it rigorously here. I also explored a direct construction via specialized complete homogeneous symmetric functions, but I could not close the argument proving regularity from the given counting condition alone.
